title: Tribuno Extra Dry Vermouth
about: Tribuno is one of the oldest American vermouths. Mario P. Tribuno was born in Turin in 1882 into a wine family and came to California in 1903 to learn grape growing and winemaking at the Italian Swiss Colony. After a career as an importer and producer, he organised Vermouth Industries of America after Repeal; the company that made Tribuno was incorporated in 1940 and blended and bottled in Manhattan, on West 45th Street, from California base wine. By the late 1970s, when the Coca-Cola Bottling Company of New York acquired it, Tribuno was the best-selling American vermouth.

In Mario Tribuno’s day, some thirty herbs and roots were macerated in wine for months and the extract aged for six months or more, then blended in small measure into base wine with sugar and citric acid. A 1951 New Yorker profile named wormwood, angelica, hyssop, orris root, sage and orange and lemon peel among them. Today Tribuno is made in California, but the brand does not publish its current producer, recipe or botanicals.

It pours pale straw, with aromas of ripe grapes, pine needles and spearmint, and it is grapey and a touch sweeter on the palate than the words “extra dry” suggest. Bottled at 16% alcohol, it is a mixing vermouth first, at home in a Martini, a Gibson or a Bronx, and in the kitchen.
facts: In a Martini, Gibson or Bronx
